description: FALSIFIER (closure predicate, carried in summary because substrateGap_write discards a free-text falsifier): the rate of 401 responses on discovery /heartbeat over a 15-minute window is zero, OR every 401 is attributable to a named vesselId that is also reported through a shaped signal (not only a journal line) within one heartbeat interval. || EVIDENCE (measured 2026-09-13 ~19:00 UTC on substrate-live): discovery's journal carries a STEADY 2 rejections per minute -- 64 in 15 minutes, 266 in an hour, 1593 in six hours, 8017 since 2026-09-12 12:00 -- each reading `[discovery] 401 POST /heartbeat — rejected: identity rejected the key (HTTP 401) (identity=http://127.0.0.1:8101)`. Exactly 2/min against the shared client's 60s heartbeat interval means TWO clients are retrying forever with a key identity rejects. identity-vessel itself has not restarted since 2026-09-09 and is active, so this is a bad credential, not an outage. || THE FAILURE IS THAT IT IS INVISIBLE. Every vessel that IS registered is fresh (all 20 rows under 60s lastSeen), so nothing in the registry looks wrong. A vessel that can never register is ABSENT, not stale -- and absence reads as 'not deployed' rather than 'broken', so no freshness check, no health probe and no ActiveState check can see it. The only signal is a journal line, and a journal line is not an escalation. Three running units are absent from the registry: discovery-vessel (by design -- it does not self-register, which is separately why bootstrap-over-libp2p needs an ingress short-circuit), identity-vessel, and boredom-vessel. || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: a sustained 401 stream is exactly what precedes a registry emptying. The federation oracle caught such an event unattended at 2026-09-12T16:45Z -- that sweep recorded I1_foreign_vantage_reachable=undecidable(registry_empty), I7_leave_propagates=undecidable(register_rejected) and I12_churn_non_destructive=FAIL(registry_lost_local_rows), coverage 0.5. The registry has since recovered on its own (13 own rows, none lost against the pre-federation baseline), so the incident was transient -- but it happened, it was only visible because an independent oracle was running, and the 401 stream that accompanies it is still going. || REPAIR DIRECTION: (1) discovery should emit a SHAPED signal naming the vesselId and the rejecting identity on repeated auth failure, not only a log line -- the same argument as emitJoinHealth existing for the transport. (2) The registration client already trips onUnhealthy after 3 consecutive failures; that callback needs a destination other than a logger. (3) Identify and re-key the two callers; a key that identity rejects indefinitely should surface as a gap, not as 2/min of journal.
